capability_set: Alias lifecycle over the API: create a random alias, create a custom alias (v2), enable or disable, delete, update.

expected.statement: An API client acts as the SimpleLogin user who owns the API key sent in the Authentication header.
A signed-in browser session can act as its user on the API when the request carries the X-Sl-Allowcookies header.
A disabled account is refused with 403, and an account whose deletion was requested is refused with 401.
A user is either on the free plan or holds a lifetime licence or an active subscription; only the free plan has an alias quota.
A user can create a random alias with POST /api/alias/random/new, with an optional note, and receives the alias with 201.
A user can create a custom alias from a prefix and a signed suffix with POST /api/v2/alias/custom/new, with an optional note, and receives the alias with 201.
A user can enable or disable an alias with POST /api/aliases/<alias_id>/toggle and receives the new status.
A user can delete an alias with DELETE /api/aliases/<alias_id>.
A user can update an alias with PUT or PATCH /api/aliases/<alias_id>: its note, name, mailbox or mailboxes, PGP setting and pinned flag.
When a hostname is given, the created alias is recorded as used on that website.
A user can delete, toggle or update only an alias they own; any other alias id is answered 403 Forbidden.
A free-plan user cannot create an alias once their aliases not pending deletion would exceed the free limit (5 by default, 15 for accounts flagged with the old limit); the request is answered 400.
A user with a lifetime licence or an active subscription has no alias count limit.
Alias creation is rate limited, by default to 100 a day, 50 an hour and 5 a minute.
Toggling an alias is limited to 100 requests an hour.
A custom alias suffix must carry a valid signature no older than 600 seconds; an invalid or expired signature is answered 412.
expected.notes: The 400 'Tampered suffix' branch is reached only when unsigning raises something other than a bad signature. A claim that a tampered suffix is answered 400 is not supported by the cited code.

expected.statement: The suffix domain must be one of the alias domains available to the user; otherwise the request is answered 400.
An address that is already an alias, or was an alias and has been deleted, cannot be created again; the request is answered 409.
An alias address may not contain two consecutive dots; the request is answered 400.

Deleting an alias moves it to the trash, disabled, for 30 days by default; an alias already in the trash, or any alias of a user who chose immediate deletion, is deleted and its address is recorded so that it cannot be reused.
An alias on a custom domain is not moved to the user's trash: it is deleted and its address is recorded in that domain's deleted aliases.
An alias can be reassigned only to a mailbox that belongs to the user and is verified; otherwise the request is answered 400.
An alias name is at most 128 characters and line breaks are removed from it.

With a hostname and the user's website setting on, a random alias request suggests an address from the website's domain name, reuses the user's own alias for that website, and never returns an alias that belongs to another user.
The mode of a random alias, when given, must be word or uuid; otherwise the request is answered 400.
A status change and an update of an alias are written to the alias audit log.
